description: A team of curious minds driven by creativity, collaboration, and a shared passion for turning ambitious ideas into meaningful innovations.
summary:
EMBERTRACE is a satellite-powered research platform designed to investigate persistent underground smouldering fires in peatlands, even after visible surface-fire activity has disappeared. The project combines NASA and other Earth-observation datasets, including NISAR synthetic aperture radar, Landsat thermal imagery, NASA FIRMS fire detections, and SMAP soil-moisture observations, to analyse changes in fire activity and peatland conditions over time.

By integrating radar observations, thermal anomalies, historical fire records, and environmental indicators, EMBERTRACE aims to identify regions showing evidence consistent with persistent underground burning and assess conditions that could favour renewed surface fires. An interactive geospatial dashboard will visualise fire history, recurring anomalies, and potential areas requiring further investigation.

The project addresses the Dancing with the SARs challenge by exploring how NISAR radar observations can contribute to monitoring environmental changes associated with peatland fires. EMBERTRACE is important because underground peat fires can remain undetected, release significant amounts of carbon, and reignite under favourable conditions. Our goal is to make these hidden threats easier to investigate and support more informed environmental monitoring and fire-management decisions.
details:
EMBERTRACE is a proposed satellite-based platform that aims to investigate persistent underground smouldering fires in peatlands, even after visible surface-fire activity disappears.

The platform could integrate multiple Earth-observation datasets, including NASA–ISRO's NISAR synthetic aperture radar observations, Landsat thermal imagery, NASA FIRMS fire detections and SMAP soil-moisture data. By analysing these complementary observations over time, it could identify regions showing patterns consistent with persistent underground smouldering and examine environmental conditions that may favour renewed surface fires.

The proposed platform would feature an interactive geospatial dashboard displaying historical fire activity, recurring thermal anomalies, radar-derived environmental changes and areas requiring further investigation.

Its potential benefits include improving awareness of hidden peatland fires, supporting environmental monitoring and helping researchers and fire-management authorities prioritise areas for investigation. The project's creative approach lies in combining radar, thermal, fire-history and environmental indicators rather than relying on individual satellite observations.

The concept considers data availability, spatial and temporal resolution, cloud interference, sensor limitations and the importance of distinguishing confirmed fire observations from suspected underground smouldering.

Proposed technologies: Python, Google Earth Engine, Rasterio, GeoPandas, React, FastAPI and Leaflet.
